approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a score-ranked survivor population. It samples preferred score quantiles, uses connected-fragment crossover and ordinary local mutation walks to fill a fresh surplus pool, then checks molecular validity, stable canonical identity and duplicates. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. An active Gaussian process uses count-Morgan features and every real accepted score from the current task; correlated posterior draws allocate the announced evaluation batch. Accepted offspring enter the full model archive and compete for the bounded greedy survivor population, so later breeding can build on earlier generated molecules.
approach.novelty: Freeze only the breeder to its ordinary initial usable, score-ranked cohort. Every later graph proposal still uses the inherited parent-draw and graph-edit rules, and the posterior continues learning from all real accepted offspring. Updated survivors remain available for incumbent tracking and reporting but cannot become breeding parents. Earlier controls removed crossover, ordinary continuation or predictive allocation; this probe preserves those mechanisms and cuts the accepted-offspring-to-breeder feedback path. It measures that recursive feedback within the current optimizer, while leaving the broader whole-optimizer question open.

hypothesis: Sever recursive accepted-offspring breeding feedback by fixing every breeding-parent draw and breeding-cohort availability check to an immutable copy of the ordinary initial usable score-ranked population, while preserving active posterior learning from all real accepted observations and the live survivor updates used for tracking and reporting.

finding_summary.headline: Recursive breeding feedback contributes: fixing initial parents lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.260206.
finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.
finding_summary.results:
Every one of 122,044 Child parent draws came from the unchanged initial cohort; no accepted offspring became a breeding parent. The Parent used accepted offspring in 105,073 of 110,295 draws. All fifteen task/seed sessions matched through their first complete batch, then diverged at the first parent, pool member and evaluated molecule of batch two. Generated offspring still entered the live survivors and the full score archive. All 435 accepted-label posterior fits and original sampled-maximum allocations remained active. All pools filled, all three seeds completed, and no natural fallback or exhaustion occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.335464, a paired change of -0.260206 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.306557, -0.273839 and -0.200221. Every one of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. Population deviation across seed macros rose from 0.026593 to 0.047795. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 2,007 against the easier fixed initial comparators, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 84. Generation also encountered more duplicate proposals: 14,385 versus 6,358.

molecular.headline: Conventional amides and aromatic frameworks recur; useful free amines emerge, but alternative useful arrangements remain uneven
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-4d4b5eafa8b3 and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch and no uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations, with complete matched Parent trajectories and identical fixed initial molecule/score records. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while every matched Parent endpoint remains higher. This is not an absence of chemical improvement over the initial observations. The evaluated Child molecules repeatedly retain recognizable indole carboxamide, polyaryl nitrile/carbonyl, pyrrolidine acid/amide and nitrogen-dione motifs. Useful scaffold rearrangements and available amines also occur, and many leaders avoid the Parent leaders' reactive N-halogen or cyclic-cumulene environments. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9517, 0.9552, 0.9034, 0.9736 and 0.8391 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9437, 0.9506, 0.8471, 0.9678 and 0.731. These are incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, despite available amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. The digest reports 639, 782, 783, 702 and 765 distinct identities across the respective Child panels. A separate check confirms 300 distinct accepted identities within every task/seed, so cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation or a failure of the budget ledger. Diversity is moderate across the recognizable molecular families and narrower among repeated leading series. The moderate drug-likeness judgement reflects familiar amide, ether, carbonyl and amine chemistry in the leaders, not strong biological performance or proved synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable for parts of the evaluated stream because of N-O/N-N ring connections, unusual sulfur or halogen environments, enlarged joined frameworks and unspecified stereochemistry. The strongest Child leaders do not universally have those liabilities; conventional-looking molecules can still have substantially lower supplied scores than questionable Parent molecules. Read-only RDKit perception supports size and functional-group descriptions; no new objective, feasibility or affinity scores were calculated. The initial observations, the frozen usable breeding cohort, and the subset actually selected as scored parents are distinct. For each retained task/seed leader, the audit joins its pool, emission and accepted-observation records and the recorded scored starting parents. The registered condition fixes initial-cohort breeding sources while retaining real accepted-label posterior allocation and live survivor updates. Source excerpts were read to interpret those records; this report does not decide activation or isolation. An unscored mutation intermediate or crossover product is not a newly scored breeding parent. A product can differ substantially from its initial sources through crossover and successive graph edits; fixed scored ancestry does not imply one atom edit or conservation of an initial scaffold. A pool member, an emitted offspring, an accepted scored molecule, a live survivor and the retained best endpoint are also different observations. The digest and chemical frequencies describe accepted trajectories, not every pool member or rejected graph. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not the best molecule of every seed. No absence from the evaluated leaders is promoted into absence from the full pool, and unselected alternatives receive no invented labels. The original n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry report and its carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index. Each transferable gap retains its original provenance and current conditions. Only digest/trusted-trajectory Child SMILES are quoted; Parent-only molecules are described by published task/seed/evaluation. Audits under .slots/r0018-02-ablation-L01/molecular/ include trajectory_audit.json, inspected_records.json, leader_provenance.json with log/source hashes, identity_scope_check.json and history_molecular_sources.json. No source or trajectory path was missing. Chemical resemblance and leader ancestry do not isolate the effect of a particular edit, membership/rank/size change or survival rule, identify mediation, or establish the contribution of the entire graph-evolution foundation. The retained predictive learning channel and live survivors prevent interpreting this condition as deletion of all feedback or the full optimizer.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules in all Child seeds are compact N-H indole carboxanilides with ordinary aryl fluorine, methoxy, methyl and sometimes methylthio substituents. They retain the recognizable aromatic/amide organization of the initial trimethoxyindole anilide, while replacing or relocating peripheral methoxy groups. A separate useful family is a phenyl/heteroaryl pyrazoline bearing a thioacyl group; the output is therefore not restricted to the indole skeleton. Mean Child SMILES length is 40.3, with a maximum of 63 and halogen-string incidence 0.754. These leading indole amides have relatively conventional bonds and no N-halogen or peroxide motif. The Parent leaders instead include an amino-substituted cumulene on N-chloro indole (seed 0, evaluation 289), an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide with N-F (seed 1, 293), and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone (seed 2, 294). The Child leaders look chemically more familiar locally, while all matched retained scores are lower. That contrast does not establish that the Parent liabilities are required.
liabilities: The leading indole amides have conventional local bonding; their limitations concern repetitive leading chemistry and unverified overall properties rather than a universal reactive-bond defect.
Thioacyl, methylthio and thiolmethyl variants require environment-specific stability assessment, while enlarged acetal-bearing or ring-opened relatives introduce additional conformational complexity.
Conventional small rings and tiny stable molecules can still score zero when the combined molecular context is absent; that is a score observation, not chemical invalidity.
missing_features: The leading set does not consistently explore distinct compact arrangements beyond variants of the initial indole amide; the useful pyrazoline family is a real exception, so there is no global inability to change scaffold.

Conventional alternative frameworks expressing the stronger Parent score associations are not demonstrated at comparable scores, but the observed ordering does not identify an exact absent pharmacophore or justify requiring N-halogen bonds.
Stereochemical identity is unresolved in the saturated pyrazoline and more complex relatives, although the flat leading indole amides themselves do not require a stereocentre assignment.

Identical or closely related evaluated molecules recur across seeds, while the stronger Parent leading arrangements are often absent from the corresponding Child leaders. Counterexamples include a useful pyrazoline thioacyl family, linked heteroaromatic recombinations, new carbonyl-ring closures and a substantially improved available-amine derivative. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically coherent alternatives that reorganize learned useful relationships under the legal task-local source and feedback rules, and assess their actual evaluated descendants. Do not equate new strings or one-edit distances with meaningful scaffold coverage. These observations cannot prescribe a benchmark-specific scaffold, show that missing chemistry was unavailable in the pool, or attribute an endpoint effect separately to membership, rank, cohort size, survival or the entire optimizer.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.

finding_summary.headline: Recursive breeding feedback contributes: fixing initial parents lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.260206.
finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.
